# TrustyHoverCard

`Overlays` · composition depth: `base`

A floating card of read-only detail, opened by hovering its trigger and dismissed when the pointer leaves. Use it to preview supplementary context — type information, metadata, a description — without interrupting the user's flow.

**Use it when**
- extra, non-essential context helps the user understand something they can see.
- use very sparingly.

**Don't use it for**
- anything interactive: no buttons, inputs, or switches. Use TrustyPopover. (The one exception is a control internal to slotted content, such as a code block's own copy button.)
- anything essential. Hover is not a reliable trigger for keyboard or touch users, so critical information must be visible by default or live in a TrustyPopover.
- a few words of hint on a control: use TrustyTooltip.
- another hover card's content: NEVER trigger one from inside one.

```ts
import { TrustyHoverCard } from '@louislp/trusty-ui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | *required* | Heading for the card. Required — a card with no title is a tooltip. |
| `description` | `string` | — | Optional supporting line beneath the title. |
| `side` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | `"top"` | Which edge of the trigger the card is anchored to |
| `alignment` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"center"` | How the card is aligned relative to the trigger |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Controlled open. Omit to open on hover after the delay. Charts bind this so the card can follow a canvas point. |

## Events

- `update:open` — `[value: boolean]`

## Slots

- `trigger`
- `default`

## Examples in Storybook

- Default — Default: title and description, no slotted content.
- TitleOnly — Title only: this should NEVER be used alone (as it's basically a TrustyTooltip).
- Right — Anchor to any edge of the trigger.
- Top
- StartAligned — Align the card to the start of the trigger.
- AttributeTable — Metadata rows in the default slot — the design's worked example. Read-only throughout: label/value pairs, no controls.
